ayurvedic_options.name: Garlic
ayurvedic_options.pros: Food-grade herb; trials and reviews report a small fall in blood pressure.
ayurvedic_options.cons: The fall is modest; smell and stomach upset are common complaints.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Adds to blood-pressure medicines and raises bleeding risk with blood thinners.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: PMID 11834913 (review of herbs and supplements in cardiovascular disease)
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of lashuna for circulatory complaints.

ayurvedic_options.name: Arjuna
ayurvedic_options.pros: Traditional cardiac tonic; animal work supports a cardiovascular effect.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Blood-pressure evidence in people is very limited and indirect.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: May add to the effect of blood-pressure-lowering medicines.
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of arjuna bark for hridroga, the heart-disease group.

ayurvedic_options.name: Moringa
ayurvedic_options.pros: Edible leaf; animal studies report lower blood pressure in metabolic syndrome models.
ayurvedic_options.cons: No human blood-pressure trials, so the size of any effect is unknown.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: May add to blood-pressure-lowering and sugar-lowering medicines.
ayurvedic_options.uses: Traditional use of shigru as food and as a metabolic tonic.

ayurvedic_options.name: Jatamansi
ayurvedic_options.pros: Traditional calming herb, used where tension and poor sleep drive blood pressure.
ayurvedic_options.cons: No human blood-pressure evidence; the record is mainly as a sedative.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Adds to drowsiness from other medicines and may add to blood-pressure lowering.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: classical Ayurvedic materia medica for Nardostachys jatamansi; this project's abstract corpus holds no cardiovascular study of it
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of jatamansi as a calming herb for the mind and the heart.

ayurvedic_options.name: Punarnava
ayurvedic_options.pros: Long traditional record as a gentle diuretic where fluid is retained.
ayurvedic_options.cons: No human blood-pressure trials; the basis is tradition alone.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: A diuretic effect can disturb fluid and potassium balance alongside heart medicines.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: classical Ayurvedic materia medica for Boerhavia diffusa; this project's abstract corpus holds no cardiovascular study of it
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of punarnava as a diuretic for shotha, fluid swelling.

ayurvedic_options.name: Sarpagandha
ayurvedic_options.pros: The best known classical Ayurvedic herb for high blood pressure.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Causes marked drowsiness, slow pulse, nasal stuffiness and low mood.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Avoid if there is depression; adds strongly to blood-pressure and heart-rate-lowering medicines.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: classical Ayurvedic materia medica for Rauvolfia serpentina, plus its well-established pharmacology; this project's abstract corpus holds no study of it
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of Indian snakeroot for raktagata vata and for unmada, mental agitation.

allopathic_options.name: Amlodipine
allopathic_options.pros: Once-daily, well tolerated, and works well in Indian and older populations.
allopathic_options.cons: Commonly causes ankle swelling; does not slow the heart rate.
allopathic_options.cautions: Ankle swelling can be mistaken for heart failure; tell the doctor if it appears.
allopathic_options.uses: Relaxing the blood vessels so blood pressure falls.

allopathic_options.name: Atenolol
allopathic_options.pros: Lowers blood pressure and the stroke and heart attack risk that comes with it.
allopathic_options.cons: Causes tiredness and cold hands; can mask the warning signs of low blood sugar.
allopathic_options.cautions: Not for people with a very slow pulse or heart block; never stop it abruptly.
allopathic_options.uses: Lowering blood pressure by slowing the heart and reducing its workload.

allopathic_options.name: Losartan
allopathic_options.pros: Well tolerated, protects the kidneys in diabetes, and rarely causes cough.
allopathic_options.cons: Can raise potassium and reduce kidney function; needs blood tests.
allopathic_options.cautions: Carries a fetal toxicity warning and must be stopped if pregnancy occurs.
allopathic_options.uses: Blocking a hormone that tightens blood vessels, so blood pressure falls.

allopathic_options.name: Metoprolol
allopathic_options.pros: Lowers blood pressure and the stroke and heart attack risk that comes with it.
allopathic_options.cons: Causes tiredness and dizziness; can mask the warning signs of low blood sugar.
allopathic_options.cautions: Not for severe slow pulse, heart block or uncontrolled heart failure; never stop abruptly.
allopathic_options.uses: Lowering blood pressure by slowing the heart and reducing its workload.

citations.evidence_sentence: T. arjuna bark extract has been reported to play a significant role as a cardiac stimulant for its beneficial effects in angina. Herb - drug interactions (HDI) are one of the most important clinical concerns in the concomitant consumption of herbs and prescription drugs. Our study was to investigate the in vitro CYP2D inhibition potential of Terminalia arjuna (T. arjuna) extracts in rat liver microsomes and to study the influence of aqueous bark extract of T. arjuna on the oral pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of metoprolol succinate in rats.

Pharmacodynamic studies reveal a significant reduction in therapeutic activity of metoprolol succinate on co-administration with aqueous bark extract of T. arjuna. Based on our in vitro and in vivo findings and until further clinical drug interaction experiments are conducted, the co-administration of drugs, especially those primarily cleared via CYP2D catalyzed metabolism, with T. arjuna extracts should be done with caution.
